unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the 0Cr steel strip (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal. (block b0018).

The average {111} planar slip band spacing measured on the cold-rolled (CR20%) 0Cr strip is 371 ± 47 nm (block b0066). This value is explicitly reported for the CR20% parent condition, not for the CR20% + annealed strip, so it is not placed in the formal structure fields of this sample.

For the as-cast 0Cr strip (not the CR20% + annealed sample): the measured volume fraction and average size of κ-carbides in γ-austenite are 3% and 6 nm; the measured lattice parameters of κ-carbides and γ-austenite are 0.387 nm and 0.375 nm; and the ordered DO3 phase in δ-ferrite has a size of 26 ± 3 nm (blocks b0048, b0053). These as-cast values are distinct from the present CR20% + annealed sample.

For the annealed (non-cold-rolled) 0Cr strip: the measured volume fraction and average size of the κ-carbides reach 7% and 8 nm respectively (block b0071). This belongs to the annealed-only process, not to the CR20% + annealed sample.

The strain hardening rate of the annealed 0Cr strip (Fig. 3(d)) exhibits a clear double-hump feature attributed to slip-band refinement (first hump) and microband formation (second hump); the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain hardening rate at the early strain stage (block b0092).

After tensile fracture the true strains of the annealed 0Cr and 6Cr strips are 0.255 and 0.298 respectively; a low-angle grain boundary with a misorientation of 2.56° was observed in the 6Cr strip (Fig. 14c, block b0088) — this misorientation is reported for the 6Cr strip, not for 0Cr.

A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening behaviour of the low-density steel strips; slip-band hardening acts at the early deformation stage and microband hardening at the final stage (blocks b0091, b0099).
